newsitem.title: UK: British entry into EMU not ruled out - govt.
newsitem.headline: British entry into EMU not ruled out - govt.

text.p: A senior government official on Monday dismissed suggestions that Prime Minister John Major's cabinet was split over whether or not Britain will join a single European currency.
The official from Major's Downing Street office said there had been no change in policy. "It is highly unlikely but not impossible that Britain can join a single currency in 1999," he said.

Health Secretary Stephen Dorrell said in a television interview on Sunday that Britain would not be joining a single currency in Janaury 1999, but he issued a statement several hours later to clarify his remarks explaining the government had not ruled out entry.
The Downing Street official said he was not aware of any call from Major to Dorrell over the statement but he added that Dorrell had obviously felt he wanted to make his position clear.

The row, which follows a similar disagreement 10 days ago when Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind said the government was hostile to a single currency only to issue a late-night statement clarifying his remarks, reopened the government's bitter split over Europe.

With only a few weeks left before the election due by May 22, Major has been desperately trying to establish unity in his party to allow him to claw back the opposition Labour Party's 20-point lead in opinion polls.
